newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Electroceramica gets Bucharest listing approval.
newsitem.headline: Electroceramica gets Bucharest listing approval.

text.p: The Bucharest stock exchange said on Friday it had given the okay to an industrial ceramics maker, whose stocks will be traded later this month.
"We approved Electroceramica's application for an exchange listing and we expect trading in this stock to start on November 20," bourse general manager Stere Farmache said.
Electroceramica SA, based in the Transylvanian town of Turda, is a state-controlled company manufacturing ceramic insulators and other electrical equipment.
The State Ownership Fund holds 70 percent of the company's 8.48 billion lei equity capital. A private ownership fund holds 13.5 percent and some 1,400 shareholders have the rest.
A company report put its annual incomes at 8.99 billion lei last year, up from 6.52 billion in 1994. It said shares had a nominal value of 25,000 lei each.
Bursa de valori Bucuresti, launched nearly one year ago, now trades 14 stocks, of which only two are privately held.
Another 21 companies have applied for listing but Farmache said it would take some time before they could join trading.
"Impact joined trading this week and another newcomer will follow soon. It looks like the bourse is gaining ground," said a broker.
Impact SA construction company joined in trading on Thursday as the bourse's second private company besides syringe maker Sanevit SA SNVT.BX. -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
